text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's microbatch size bump from 2 -> 4 on the chatstream pool, we're seeing a p99 tail increase of ~30ms on several rtx instances. Non-streaming completions pools look flat. Anyone else observing this? :eyes:

jonathan: I saw the alert. Reproduced on my local sim with traffic replay. p50 unchanged, p95 +10ms, p99 +30-40ms. Looks like extra tail work per token.

liam: Share profiler traces? My first guess is the kernel selector or KV cache handshakes getting more contended when mbsize changes.

zoe: Pasting a small profiler snippet from a failed request (streaming path):
```
trace_id=abc123 kernel_select: model=redwood-chat-v0 seq_len=48 mb_size=4 selected_kernel=attn_v2 latency_est=6.2ms
kv_cache: lookup=miss (prefix_miss) fetch_remote=8.1ms wait_queue=12.4ms tail_work=22.9ms
stream_write: chunked=true flush_delay=5.0ms
```
Noting the wait_queue + tail_work numbers blow up vs mbsize=2 runs.

maria: That matches what I saw in aggregated histograms — tail mass moves into a longer "post-token" region when mbsize grows. Completions path doesn't use streaming flush, so it avoids that micro-tail.

nora: Could be the handshake backpressure: streaming keeps the connection open and we flush partial chunks; when mbsize bigger we schedule larger microbatches which increases kv access overlap and causes a small surge of eviction/deserialize work.

jonathan: I dug into kernel chooser logs. With mbsize=4 we're selecting `kv_stream_opt_v2` for ~65% of calls, whereas mbsize=2 mostly picks `kv_stream_opt_v1`. v2 has better steady throughput but higher worst-case prep time (kernel init + warmup) under KV miss.

liam: Interesting — so kernel selection is tipping the tradeoff. v2 reduces avg tokens/sec but increases tail when a rare kv-miss happens. Do we have per-kernel p99 breakdown?

perf-bot: Per-kernel p99 (last 6h) for chatstream pools: attn_v1 p99=84ms, attn_v2 p99=125ms, kv_stream_opt_v1 p99=92ms, kv_stream_opt_v2 p99=156ms.

zoe: QE replay: I ran synthetic with same request mix and forced KV cache cold-starts. With mbsize=4 the tail coupling is much worse (kv_stream_opt_v2 stalls on deserialization). With mbsize=2 the effect is present but smaller.

maria: Quick mitigation — I rolled back mbsize to 2 for the chat pool at 09:12 via `deploy-bot` and p99 dropped back to baseline within 2 mins. Reverting for completions not necessary.

deploy-bot: Rollout event: set-mbsize pool=chatstream from=4 to=2 triggered by maria at 2024-06-15T09:12:43Z.

jonathan: Can we do a targeted policy: keep mbsize=4 for completions and for chatstream use adaptive mbsize (2 baseline, allow 3/4 when KV hit rate > 95%)? That keeps throughput when cache is hot but avoids tail during cache churn.

liam: Implementation note: need a cheap per-pool sliding window for KV hit rate and a throttled adapter to avoid oscillation. Add hysteresis: only scale up after sustained 30s window and scale down immediately on p99 alert.

nora: Also consider making kernel chooser prefer kv_stream_opt_v1 for chatstream until we can tune v2's deserialization path. Quick patch suggestion: add a kernel-score penalty for kernels with observed p99 > threshold in last 10m.

zoe: Agree. I can instrument the deserializer to avoid per-request allocations (suspect that's the deserialization stall). If we can shave 5-10ms off deserial, v2 p99 should come down.

maria: Action list: 1) Zoe to prototype deserializer micro-optimizations (ETA EOD). 2) Jonathan + Liam to add adaptive mbsize policy and kernel-score fallback (ETA 2 days). 3) Nora to add an emergency kernel-penalty knob we can flip from console (ETA 1 day). 4) Perf team to run long-running replay with mixed hot/cold cache to validate.

jonathan: I'll also add an automated A/B test for new kernel versions that measures p50/p95/p99 separately and gates by p99 impact > +5ms.

liam: For immediate SLO safety, let's add a guard in the routing layer: if pool p99 for streaming exceeds threshold, force mbsize=2 and prefer low-tail kernels. This can be a temporary circuit breaker.

maria: Sounds good. One more datapoint: the extra tail correlates with sequences that trigger prefix cache misses ~0.6% of requests. So it's rare but high cost. Need to reduce tail causally, not just hide it.

zoe: Will push a small profiler build that traces allocation hotspots in deserializer and a config flag to disable streaming flush coalescing as an experiment.

nora: I'll expose the kernel-penalty toggle in the console UI under runtime -> safety -> kernel overrides so SRE can flip it in incidents.

maria: Thanks all. If someone hits a repro test, drop the perf trace here. I'll keep the chat pool at mbsize=2 until we confirm fixes. :thumbsup:

jonathan: Dropping a quick repro command for others to run locally:
```bash
./replay --pool chatstream --mbsize 4 --traffic-pattern chat-mix.json --kv-cold-rate 0.6 --duration 5m > trace.log
```

liam: ran that locally, attached small snippet — will upload to S3 and link in a follow-up thread.

perf-bot: Note: p99 alert cleared for chatstream at 2024-06-15T09:18:05Z after rollback.

maria: follow-up: create a small dashboard showing kernel distribution, per-kernel p99, and kv hit-rate for chat vs completions. That should make regressions easier to spot.

zoe: ack, will add a panel to the runtime dashboard and include the deserial flamegraph once available.

maria: closing loop for now — chat pool remains at mbsize=2, completions stay at 4. We'll reconvene once Zoe's perf patch or the adaptive mbsize landed.

jonathan: thanks, good triage.

liam: +1

nora: +1 (and I've set an incident runbook note about kernel-penalty toggle).
